sources.note: Finds that few-shot chain-of-thought prompting with dataset examples now performs worse than simply asking a reasoning-specialized model the question — 74.2% against 86.1% on GSM8K for one model — so the field's standard baseline systematically understates modern models and overstates anything benchmarked against it.
sources.title: Soft Guidance Starts to Outperform CoT Prompting as LLMs Improve

sources.note: Trains a difference-of-means direction on short- versus long-horizon answer continuations and steers along it, shifting binary temporal choices, moving the monetary indifference threshold on an untrained task by a factor of 56 at a ten-year delay, and changing a planning benchmark — with matched-norm random controls and an unusually candid account of what the direction may actually encode.
sources.title: Intertemporal Preference Steering in Qwen3 via Contrastive Activation Addition

sources.note: Formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over a model's implicit prefix tree, separates three structurally different regimes that a single scalar budget conflates, specifies what a reproducible inference protocol must declare, and releases 1.9 million traces — with the empirical section showing a selection score that makes accuracy fall from 75.56% to 65.83% as the candidate bank grows.
sources.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility

sources.note: Turns table-to-report generation into Monte Carlo tree search over partial reports, scored by a reward that verifies every numerical claim by generating and executing SQL against the source table rather than by asking a judge — and keeps that search reward strictly separate from the benchmark's own evaluator to avoid a reward-hacking loop.
sources.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Table-to-Multimodal Report Generation

sources.note: Decomposes measured self-correction gains into a content margin and format-recovery margins, and shows causally that most of what the field has reported as self-correction is answer-parseability repair.
sources.title: The Calibration Floor: Format Repair Can Masquerade as Self-Correction at Small-to-Mid Scale

sources.note: Tests reasoning models on Theory of Mind tasks and argues their gains are increased robustness to prompt and task perturbation rather than a new ToM-specific ability.
sources.title: Evaluating Theory of Mind in Reasoning Models: Robustness over Reasoning

sources.note: An Italian proverb benchmark on which models complete proverbs successfully but fail multiple-choice selection when no correct option is present, with CoT analysis showing they name the right ending while failing to notice its absence.
sources.title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark

sources.note: Measures not how far six frontier models move under steering pressure but what kind of response they give when they decline, finds several response modes belonging to a single model, and then traces the largest within-model split to a linearly decodable and causally steerable direction in an open-weight model's residual stream.
sources.title: Divergent Response Modes in Frontier Language Models Under Steering Pressure

sources.note: Shows that the standard metric for judging contamination-mitigation strategies can be scored by cancellation rather than by restoration, replaces it with a per-question stratified metric under which the published ranking reverses, and proposes a mitigation that decides its intervention during decoding instead of from a prior estimate.
sources.title: Zero Gap Is Not Restoration: Stratified Per-Question Probability Evaluation and Step-wise Mitigation of Benchmark Contamination

sources.note: Trains an open-weight model with GRPO against a safety-gated LLM-as-a-judge rubric for financial advice, then audits the result with a judge-independent causal estimator on logged outcomes -- and finds the two evaluations rank the other systems differently, with the untrained base model last on the rubric and second on the audit.
sources.title: GRPO for Financial Advice Generation: Outperforming Commercial LLMs under CATE Evaluation

sources.note: Decomposes mathematical problem-solving into four cognitive dimensions after Polya and tests each separately, finding wide capability gaps that final-answer accuracy hides.
sources.title: SMART: Evaluating LLMs' Mathematical Reasoning via a Human Cognitive Process-Inspired Benchmark

sources.note: Benchmarks whether multimodal models can construct visual aids for geometry problems, and finds high answer accuracy conceals near-total failure at producing or reasoning from those aids.
sources.title: VisAidMath: Benchmarking Visual-Aided Mathematical Reasoning

sources.note: Consolidates multiword-expression resources into one evaluation suite covering idioms, noun compounds and verbal constructions across extraction, classification and interpretation tasks.
sources.title: Revisiting a Pain in the Neck: A Semantic Reasoning Benchmark for Language Models

sources.note: A university-level multimodal math benchmark with original, hand-drawn, photographed and text-only variants of each problem, on which a model with no image beats its own multimodal variants and GPT-5.
sources.title: MathSight: A Benchmark Exploring Have Vision-Language Models Really Seen in University-Level Mathematical Reasoning?

sources.note: A competitive chess testbed where 13 models play each other, and no model beats a human-amateur-level engine while some lose to random play.
sources.title: ChessArena: A Chess Testbed for Evaluating Strategic Reasoning Capabilities of Large Language Models

sources.note: A benchmark where each task needs one commonsense step and one math step, on which model accuracy drops nearly 30% relative to solving the steps in isolation while humans show no such gap.
sources.title: AgentCoMa: A Compositional Benchmark Mixing Commonsense and Mathematical Reasoning in Real-World Scenarios

sources.note: Uses 200 mathematical proof problems as a diagnostic, finding some reasoning models solve under 20% and cataloguing 10 fine-grained error types that numerical benchmarks hide.
sources.title: Mathematical Proof as a Litmus Test: Revealing Failure Modes of Advanced Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: A financial reasoning benchmark built from parameterized symbolic templates with executable Python, giving machine-verifiable step-level ground truth and contamination-free regeneration.
sources.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning

sources.note: Separates perception from reasoning in ARC-style benchmarks with a two-stage pipeline, and finds about 80% of vision-language model failures are perception errors, not reasoning errors.
sources.title: Your Reasoning Benchmark May Not Test Reasoning: Revealing Perception Bottleneck in Abstract Reasoning Benchmarks

sources.note: A fully automated multi-turn reasoning benchmark of 40 tasks and 3600 instances requiring interaction with an environment, on which frontier reasoning models fall short.
sources.title: MTR-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Multi-Turn Reasoning Evaluation

sources.note: A business-domain benchmark pairing four knowledge areas with three practitioner roles, designed to trace application performance back to the theoretical capability it depends on.
sources.title: BizCompass: Benchmarking the Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs in Business Knowledge and Applications

sources.note: Benchmarks multimodal models on detecting and categorizing errors in K-12 math solutions collected from real student interactions, with the best model about 10% behind human experts.
sources.title: ErrorRadar: Benchmarking Complex Mathematical Reasoning of Multimodal Large Language Models Via Error Detection

sources.note: An inductive-reasoning benchmark from historical linguistics that requires inducing cascades of string-rewrite programs, with automated contamination-resistant generation and controllable difficulty.
sources.title: PBEBench: A Multi-Step Programming by Examples Reasoning Benchmark inspired by Historical Linguistics

sources.note: Evaluates code reasoning by implementation invariance and intermediate-state accuracy, finding models get final outputs right while reasoning incorrectly about execution.
sources.title: CoRE: A Fine-Grained Code Reasoning Benchmark Beyond Output Prediction

sources.note: Shows that when a rating task admits several defensible interpretations, forcing raters to pick one answer biases LLM-as-a-judge validation so badly that the selected judge can be up to 31% worse than the one chosen by asking raters for the set of all plausible ratings.
sources.title: Validating LLM-as-a-Judge Systems under Rating Indeterminacy

sources.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
sources.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

sources.note: Builds a large standardized meta-benchmark and finds that LLM-judge preference scores do not correlate with concrete measures of safety, world knowledge or instruction following, because judges systematically prioritize style over factuality and safety.
sources.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking

sources.note: Evaluates 21 LLM judges across three benchmarks and three protocols over ~541,000 judgments, and shows the field's standard validation metric — exact-match agreement — overstates chance-corrected discrimination by 34-41 points universally, while high test-retest reliability can coexist with severe position bias.
sources.title: Reliability without Validity: A Systematic, Large-Scale Evaluation of LLM-as-a-Judge Models Across Agreement, Consistency, and Bias

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'construct validity'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:
- Write in en.
- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.
- No marketing language. Prefer the specific number over the adjective.
- Return one JSON object matching the schema exactly. No prose around it.

aliases: string - other names the sources use for the same thing
output_schema.definition: string - two to four sentences defining the entity as the cited sources use it, not as a textbook would
output_schema.kind: string - one of: concept, method, dataset, model
related: string - name of a neighbouring entity worth linking to. Kept as you give it and never derived away, so name what a reader should turn to next rather than what happens to appear alongside this. Answering again replaces the whole list; an empty list retracts

result.definition: Whether a measurement is measuring the thing it is named after, and across 28 sources the archive's most frequently applied critical lens -- usually applied by the authors to their own work, which is why it appears in limitations more often than in results. The recurring failure is a correlated alternative that the design cannot exclude. A temporal-horizon steering direction also separates abstraction, urgency, strategic scope and framing, so the intervention may be steering a broad answer register rather than the named variable, and a transfer result shows the construct is involved without identifying the direction's semantic basis. A probe's margin can be generic: training the identical probe on a small model that never produced the responses reaches 0.72 because the items are by construction more ambiguous as prompts, so only the 14-point margin above that is unexplained. And a total-effect measurement can be answering a different question entirely -- a revision that turns an unparseable output into a parseable one changes the score without changing any reasoning. Two conclusions the corpus reaches are worth carrying. Validity is a property of the whole protocol rather than of the model: measured performance depends on template, decoder, controller, reducer, verifier, stopping rule and numerical settings, so a number without its protocol is not comparable to another. And some constructs have no clean measurement window at all -- one source shows that models weak enough to have headroom lack the signal while models with the signal lack the headroom, leaving the design space where the construct could be measured cleanly nearly empty.
